key_insight: WebHarbor brings realistic web interactions into controlled environments through 153 executable, Docker-packaged website reconstructions. It aims to give GUI agents realistic websites without the instability of live-web testing.
problem_solved: Live websites change, restrict access, and limit evaluation of authenticated workflows. Synthetic training environments often lack the visual fidelity and functional depth needed to develop capable GUI agents.
method: Build a suite of 153 executable website environments.
Reconstruct real websites’ visual interfaces, content, and functionality.
Package environments with Docker to support controlled deployment for GUI-agent evaluation and training.
impact: WebHarbor could make GUI-agent evaluation more reproducible and training more realistic. The provided abstract is truncated, so performance improvements and detailed validation results are not available.
visual_elements: Split-screen comparison: changing live website versus controlled Docker-hosted reconstruction.
Pipeline diagram: real website → reconstruction → Docker container → GUI agent.
Grid of website thumbnails with a prominent “153 environments” label.
Icons highlighting visual fidelity, interactivity, and reproducibility.
paper_title: WebHarbor: Docking Real Websites for Evolving GUI Agent Environments
paper_authors: Zhaoyang Wang, Qianhui Wu, Boyu Gou, Demi Wang, Jiacheng Zhang
